name: Crab Nebula
tagline: The wreckage of a star seen exploding in 1054 — still expanding.
history: In July 1054, Chinese and Japanese astronomers recorded a 'guest star' bright enough to read by at night and visible in daylight for 23 days. Six centuries later Charles Messier catalogued its remnant — the object that inspired his famous list of comet look-alikes as entry M1. At its heart spins the Crab pulsar, a 30-km neutron star rotating 30 times per second and beaming radiation like a lighthouse across every wavelength. The expanding filaments now span about 11 light-years; comparing photographs across decades shows the debris still racing outward — an explosion in progress.

images.caption: NASA's Hubble Captures the Beating Heart of the Crab Nebula
